correctness.rationale: With the inner product linear in its first slot, the conjugate angular mode gives the sole lower off-diagonal moment 2ε B(2n+2,1+α+iτ); all diagonals are unchanged. Projection of z^n onto the lower-degree space is therefore entirely in the q_(n−1) direction. For monic norms the exact recursion t_n=1−n(n+1)|γ_n|²/t_(n−1), t_n=(n+1)h_n, and the lower bound t_n≥1−2|ε| give the quadratic leading-coefficient term with positive sign. The gamma quotient gives a_n=γ_n/h_(n−1)=A n^(−α−iτ)(1+O(n^−1+n^−(2α))). On the full exterior |1/z|≤1 and a_n→0, so the monic ratio recursion is uniformly bounded and one substitution gives the −a_n/z term with O(n^−(2α)) error. The full replacement error in Step 4 is O(n^(−α−1)+n^(−3α)), not in general just O(n^(−α−1)); both terms are absorbed by the proved remainder. Homogeneity and boundedness of (1−t^(α−iτ))/(1−t)^α on [0,1) give the Hölder extension. Gamma has no zeros, and for τ≠0 rounding exp((2πm+θ)/|τ|) gives subsequences approaching every prescribed phase; τ=0 gives the single stated limit.
residual_risks: The frozen mpmath checks were read, not rerun. They test only α=0.6, τ=1.2, ε=0.2 and selected degrees; the independent analytic check, not the recorded numerical output, supports the theorem.

evidence: Hübner Theorem A gives O(N^−β) for β<α on exterior sets separated from the boundary; for regularity index 0 the stated bound on sets meeting the boundary has a half-power loss. Theorem B concerns a truncated collar approximation.
Hedenmalm–Wennman Theorem 1.2.1 gives all-order expansions with a fixed real-analytic weight; that hypothesis fails at |z|=1 here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The finite-regularity theorem covers the leading factor in its applicable region but not the endpoint coefficients or the oscillatory law. The stronger analytic expansion does not cover the weight.

evidence: An O(n^−β) error for each β<α is compatible with an identically zero error or with nonzero n^−α oscillations and does not give the quadratic coefficient of κ_n.
The exact gamma phase follows from the conjugate angular Fourier mode and the beta moment of this particular area weight; the circle tridiagonal calculation does not have that moment.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known tools and the leading factor are credited. None of the inspected results already gives the claimed law by specialization.

value.rationale: The example gives an actual obstruction to improving the rate to little-o(n^−α) from Hölder regularity and constant boundary trace alone, even at a single fixed exterior point. The separation of the leading-coefficient and exterior scales, and the optional phase oscillation, give a benchmark for endpoint claims that a generic rate estimate cannot supply.
residual_risks: One model weight only: this does not prove an endpoint upper bound for all Hölder weights or all domains.
